questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've heard a lot of positive feedback from my peers in terms of their experience abroad in Heidelberg and the university itself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was centered around the mobility platform, which made it more easy to grasp, although it was a bit difficult overall.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I, as well as the other international students, received a welcoming from the tutors at the university. There were a lot of different events, that you could attend to both to be informed about the faculties as well as to meet other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
My friend and I looked for a furnished apartment.
Wunderflats.com
is a great website to search on for that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a bit more quiet - we lived in a very family friendly area, which was nice, when we wanted a bit more space and quiet around us. But I wouldn't do that on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got all the information we needed from the beginning by attending the first introduction week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mainly the tutors and the overall administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got in on all the classes I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can alway write an e-mail when in doubt. There are a lot of people, who work in the international department and are ready to help at all times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to do a lot more reading than usual during the semester - but I found it all very exciting so I really enjoyed it, although it was challenging at times.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit more analogue and some seminars were really discussion-based, which you had to prepare a lot for by yourself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
"P1: Einführung in die Philosophie". 
"Einführung in die Literaturwissenschaft".
"Goethe: Die Wahlverwandtschaften". 
"Die Wut, die bleibt - Simone de Beauvoir im zeitgenössischen Feminismus".

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"Einführung in die Literaturwissenschaft".
This programm is great for both beginners and for non-beginners at studying literature; you really get to apply a lot of general knowledge about literary theories and it introduces a big rage of text material - both novels, short stories, poems and plays. The class is an open space for discussions and you probably won't be the only Erasmus student attending.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the community around UCPH more easy to enter into. You have to look a bit more for it at Heidelberg University, as it isn't as centered as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, summer parties (organized by the student council) and other social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the parties and social events, where you get to meet a lot of new people and build a network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going outside from the city and experience new locations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. People were really welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most people are really sweet if you just come up and say hi.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The whole atmosphere around attending university and studying.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to choose courses around campus; not just at one faculty. 
2. Be a tourist! The city is amazing and a must to experience. 
3. Don't be afraid to talk to non-Erasmus students in class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Proving that I could do it for myself; live and study in a foreign city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to build up some confidence at first using my language. I found that really challenging in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
